pass_b_english: Cyril: …to their vanities, to which they themselves will fornicate away after them.’ So then he denies altogether the sacrificing indiscriminately, to whichever someone should wish, and that the worships must be finished for the God by nature alone, he says very well.
Palladius: How most excellently the word holds for us.

Cyril: And it would also benefit us not moderately in another manner I think to think that it is profitable and somehow already necessary that the sacrifices must be practiced in the holy tent alone, and the sacred victims be brought forward.
Cyril: Or were we not saying that the calf being slaughtered beside the holy tent concerning both priest and ignorances of people is an image and type of Emmanuel?

Cyril: So then we say that in this way the mystery of Christ must be finished in holy tents, the Churches of God. For this again he was typing for us also elsewhere. For having legislated in beginnings in what manner the lamb must be slaughtered unto a type of Christ for those from Israel departing land of Egyptians: ‘In one house it will be eaten,’ he says, ‘and you will not carry out from its meats outside.’ So then the differently-minded heretics undo what seems good to God, pitching another tent for themselves beside the tent that is truly holy, and sacrificing the lamb outside, and carrying it away somewhere farthest from the one house, and dividing the undivided; for one and perfect in all is Christ. But wise and hierophant Moses for us also charges saying in the Deuteronomy, ‘Take heed to yourself lest you bring up your whole-burnt-offering in every place which you should see, but unto a place which Lord your God should choose it, in one of your cities, there you will bring up your whole-burnt-offerings, and there you will do all things as many as I command you today…’ So then a fault and writing of the most abominable mind is to dare to sacrifice in every place, and not to fulfill the mystery of Christ in house of God.
Palladius: You speak well; yet speak that. The law has adulterated the eating of blood, and very reasonably. And what again would the mind in at least the letter be?

Cyril: So then, if it seems good, come let us also say the things oracled upon this, also in the Leviticus. For it holds thus: ‘And the human of the sons of Israel, or of the proselytes attached among you, who should eat every blood, I will set my face upon the soul eating the blood, and I will destroy it from its people. For the soul of every flesh is its blood
